reconstructed_theorem_text:
Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner-product space equipped with its Borel measurable structure. Let (A,mu) be any measurable probability space. Let V:E->R be C^2 and kappa be a nonnegative real with 1<=kappa, and assume that for every x,v in E,
  kappa^(-1)||v||^2 <= D^2 V(x)[v,v] <= ||v||^2.
Let eta,c,epsilon be real numbers with 0<eta<=c<1 and epsilon>0. Fix arbitrary functions q:E->E and N:E->N such that for every y in E,
  run(grad V,eta,epsilon,y,N(y)+1,y)=some(q(y),N(y)+1).
Here the finite interpreter run(g,eta,epsilon,y,fuel,x) returns none at zero fuel. With positive fuel it evaluates g(x) and sets next=y-eta g(x). It returns (x,1) when ||next-x||<=(1-eta)epsilon; otherwise it recurses from next with fuel decreased by one and adds one to a successful returned query count. Arithmetic is exact real arithmetic. Consequently N(y)+1 is the reported number of gradient tests, including the final successful test, for this successful run initialized at y.
For every measurable Y:A->E such that omega -> ||grad V(Y(omega))||^2 is integrable with respect to mu, the real-valued test count omega -> N(Y(omega))+1 is integrable with respect to mu, and
  integral_A (N(Y(omega))+1) dmu(omega)
    <= [2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c)]
       [1+log(1+sqrt(integral_A ||grad V(Y(omega))||^2 dmu(omega))/epsilon)].
Natural counts in this formula are cast to the reals. Integrability is Bochner integrability. The logarithm is the real logarithm and the square root is the real square root. The conclusions concern the integrability and expected count of the stipulated successful exact-arithmetic interpreter; no existence of q or N, explicit pointwise complexity bound, output-error guarantee, sampling-kernel property, or convergence statement is asserted by this theorem.
objects: A real inner-product space E, measurable probability space (A,mu), C^2 potential V, Hessian quadratic form D^2 V(x)[v,v], gradient grad V, nonnegative-real curvature parameter kappa, real eta/c/epsilon, arbitrary functions q:E->E and N:E->N recording a successful finite interpreter output and its count minus one, measurable input Y:A->E, its squared-gradient moment M=integral ||grad V(Y)||^2 dmu, and the real test-count random variable N(Y)+1. The interpreter run is the exact-real anchored iteration and residual test given in the approved definition context.
domains: E has NormedAddCommGroup, InnerProductSpace R, CompleteSpace, FiniteDimensional R, MeasurableSpace, and BorelSpace structures. A is any type with a MeasurableSpace structure. mu is a probability measure on A. V:E->R; kappa belongs to the nonnegative reals; eta,c,epsilon belong to R. q:E->E and N:E->N. Y:A->E. Both the squared-gradient function and the real count N(Y)+1 are functions A->R integrated against mu. There is no finite-index type, Gaussian law, or transition-state space in this statement.
quantifiers: For every E and A with the specified structures, every probability measure mu on A, every V and kappa satisfying the smoothness and Hessian hypotheses, every eta/c/epsilon satisfying the parameter inequalities, and every q,N satisfying the displayed successful-run equality for all y in E: for every measurable Y:A->E whose squared-gradient norm is integrable, both count integrability and the displayed integral inequality hold. The Hessian inequalities are universal in x and v. q and N are fixed universally quantified inputs to this implication, not existential conclusions. The run hypothesis applies to every y, while the moment and integration conclusions concern the chosen Y and mu.
assumptions: mu has total mass one. V is C^2 over R. kappa is nonnegative and 1<=kappa. For every x,v, kappa^(-1)||v||^2<=D^2 V(x)[v,v]<=||v||^2. Parameters satisfy 0<eta, eta<=c, c<1, and epsilon>0; in particular 0<c<1 follows. For every y, the run initialized at x=y with anchor y and fuel N(y)+1 returns exactly some(q(y),N(y)+1). Y is measurable and omega -> ||grad V(Y(omega))||^2 is Bochner integrable with respect to mu. No measurability of q or N is separately assumed. No boundedness of Y, independence, Gaussian input, or additional epsilon upper bound is assumed.
conclusion: The real-valued function omega -> (N(Y(omega)):R)+1 is Bochner integrable, and its integral is at most C(c)*(1+log(1+sqrt(M)/epsilon)), where C(c)=2+(1+log((1-c)^(-1)))/(-log c) and M=integral ||grad V(Y(omega))||^2 dmu(omega). The count includes every evaluated gradient test, including the terminal successful test. The formula uses the square root of the integrated squared-gradient norm, not the integral of the gradient norm or the integral of its logarithm.
scopes: The all-y run equality is a hypothesis about global witness functions q,N. The theorem establishes integrability and an expected-count bound under each chosen probability law mu and measurable Y with finite squared-gradient moment. Integrability supplies the corresponding measure-theoretic measurability/integrability property of the real count composition; the theorem does not state that N is everywhere measurable on E or that q is measurable. It does not conclude existence of q,N, an explicit pointwise bound for every y, accuracy of q relative to an implicit solution, existence or invariance of a Markov kernel, convergence of a sampler, or finite-precision implementation guarantees.
constant_dependencies: The displayed multiplicative constant C(c) depends only on c. The logarithmic factor depends on epsilon and M=integral ||grad V(Y)||^2 dmu, hence on V,Y,mu through that moment. eta and kappa occur in the hypotheses but not separately in the displayed bound. The bound has no explicit dependence on dim(E), q, or the individual values of N apart from the left-hand expected count. q,N must satisfy the exact run equation for the fixed V,eta,epsilon. The assumptions imply -log c>0 and (1-c)>0, so the constant is defined with positive denominator and positive logarithm argument; M is nonnegative because its integrand is nonnegative.
